\begin{theorem}[Absolute value of an indexed sign monomial]
\lean{FABL.abs_indexedMonomial_eq_one}
\label{FABL.abs_indexedMonomial_eq_one}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.IndexedSignCube, FABL.indexedMonomial, FABL.indexedMonomial_sq}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\iota$ be an index set, let $S\subseteq\iota$ be finite, and assign a sign to
each index in $\iota$. The absolute value of the product of the signs indexed by $S$ is
$1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier norm under a coordinate split]
\lean{FABL.sum_abs_split_fourierCoeff_eq_fourierOneNorm}
\label{FABL.sum_abs_split_fourierCoeff_eq_fourierOneNorm}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FixedIndex, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.fourierOneNorm, FABL.frequencySplitEquiv, FABL.frequencySplitEquiv_apply, FABL.liftFixedFrequency, FABL.liftFreeFrequency}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional
sign cube, and let $J$ be a subset of its coordinates. Sum the absolute values of the
Fourier coefficients indexed by the union of a subset of $J$ and a subset of its
complement, over all choices of both subsets. This sum equals the Fourier one-norm of
$f$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Two expressions for restricted Fourier weight]
\lean{FABL.restrictedFourierWeight_equation6_6}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p084-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p084-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p077-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p076-b004
}
\label{FABL.restrictedFourierWeight_equation6_6}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FixedIndex, FABL.FixedSignCube, FABL.expect_sq_restrictionFourierCoeff, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.liftFixedFrequency, FABL.liftFreeFrequency, FABL.mean, FABL.restrictedFourierWeight, FABL.restrictionFourierCoeff}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional
sign cube, let $J$ be a finite set of coordinates, and let $S$ be a finite subset of
$J$. The restricted Fourier weight equals the sum, over all subsets $T$ of the
coordinates outside $J$, of the squared Fourier coefficients at the union of the lifted
frequency sets from $S$ and $T$; moreover, this sum equals the uniform mean over sign
assignments outside $J$ of the squared restricted Fourier coefficient.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier norm of a sign restriction]
\lean{FABL.sum_abs_indexedFourierCoeff_signRestriction_le_fourierOneNorm}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p086-b007}
\label{FABL.sum_abs_indexedFourierCoeff_signRestriction_le_fourierOneNorm}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FixedIndex, FABL.FixedSignCube, FABL.abs_indexedMonomial_eq_one, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.fourierOneNorm, FABL.indexedFourierCoeff, FABL.indexedMonomial, FABL.liftFixedFrequency, FABL.liftFreeFrequency, FABL.restrictionFourierCoeff, FABL.restrictionFourierCoeff_eq_sum, FABL.signRestriction, FABL.sum_abs_split_fourierCoeff_eq_fourierOneNorm}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional
sign cube, let $J$ be a subset of its coordinates, and fix signs $z$ outside $J$. The
sum of the absolute values of all Fourier coefficients of the restriction of $f$ to the
free coordinates in $J$, with the outside coordinates fixed to $z$, is at most the
Fourier one-norm of $f$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier norm of restriction coefficients]
\lean{FABL.sum_abs_indexedFourierCoeff_restrictionFourierCoeff_le_fourierOneNorm}
\label{FABL.sum_abs_indexedFourierCoeff_restrictionFourierCoeff_le_fourierOneNorm}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FixedIndex, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.fourierOneNorm, FABL.indexedFourierCoeff, FABL.indexedFourierCoeff_restrictionFourierCoeff, FABL.liftFixedFrequency, FABL.liftFreeFrequency, FABL.restrictionFourierCoeff, FABL.sum_abs_split_fourierCoeff_eq_fourierOneNorm}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional
sign cube, let $J$ be a subset of its coordinates, and let $S$ be a subset of $J$.
Regard the Fourier coefficient of the restriction of $f$ with free-coordinate frequency
$S$ as a function of the signs fixed outside $J$. The Fourier one-norm, on the cube of
fixed coordinates, of this coefficient function is at most the Fourier one-norm of $f$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Reindexing a fixed sign cube]
\lean{FABL.fixedSignCubeEquiv}
\label{FABL.fixedSignCubeEquiv}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FixedIndex, FABL.FixedSignCube}
Let $n$ be a natural number and $J$ a set of coordinates in $\bbr^n$ represented by a
finite subset of $\bbr^n$. The space of sign assignments to the coordinates outside $J$
is bijective to the space of sign vectors of length equal to the number of those
remaining coordinates, by reindexing the coordinates.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier norm after reindexing a coefficient function]
\lean{FABL.fourierOneNorm_restrictionFourierCoeff_comp_fixedSignCubeEquiv_eq}
\label{FABL.fourierOneNorm_restrictionFourierCoeff_comp_fixedSignCubeEquiv_eq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FixedIndex, FABL.fixedSignCubeEquiv, FABL.fourierCoeff_restrictionFourierCoeff_comp_fixedSignCubeEquiv, FABL.fourierOneNorm, FABL.indexedFourierCoeff, FABL.restrictionFourierCoeff}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, let $J$ be a set
of coordinates, and let $S\subseteq J$. For each assignment $z$ of signs outside $J$,
take the Fourier coefficient indexed by $S$ of the restriction of $f$ to $J$; this gives
a real-valued function of $z$. The Fourier one-norm of this function, with the outside
coordinates reindexed by a cube of the same dimension, equals the sum of the absolute
values of its Fourier coefficients indexed by subsets of the outside-coordinate set.
\end{theorem}
